To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of data compression algorithms in conjunction with a probability model to calculate the reliability index can be used to reduce the data redundancy in a wireless sensor network and also provide a reliability index for the network as a whole.

our proposed method is a simple and effective way to compress data at the local cluster heads, and to calculate the reliability index at the central coordinator, without the need of any calibration values and threshold.

the proposed method can reduce the amount of data sent to the central coordinator by 80% and the reliability of data can be increased to a value of 90% by using the reference PMax value at the cluster heads to compare the reliability of individual sensor nodes and the global reliability index at the central coordinator.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reliability of sensor readings in large sensor networks and how to use the reliability of the sensors in the network to improve the data reliability in the network.
developing a reliable sensor network which is scalable and energy efficient by using data compression and a reliability index.
the development of a reliable sensor network which is scalable and energy efficient and can be used for a wide range of applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach is a reliable and scalable method to compress data in a wireless sensor network which can be applied independent of the application type.

the proposed algorithm is a reliable and scalable solution to the problem of data compression and reliability for large scale sensor networks and it is a good candidate for further investigation and implementation.
the proposed solution is an energy-efficient and reliable solution to large-scale wireless sensor networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the data compression algorithm and the PMax index are used to reduce the network overhead in large scale sensor networks by using the probability model of the data and a reliability index which is independent of the application and the measured values and is used to compare and correct the data at the cluster head and the central coordinator respectively.
the proposed solution is a generic solution to the reliability issue of sensor network which is application independent.
we use a global reliability index based upon the PMax calculated at the cluster head to compare the local reliability index of the individual cluster head.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the reliability index is independent of the actual data values and the reliability is based only on the probability model which is based on the current lifetime of the network and the data redundancy of the sensors.
the reliability of the network is more important than the reliability of the individual sensors as the sensor readings are only used to calculate the network reliability.

we can use this PM ax to estimate the global reliability of a sensor network and use it as a reliability threshold to compare with the current reliability of the sensor network to decide on the need to re-calibrate the network or not and hence reduce energy consumption.
